extracted.intended_audience: students of mathematical logic (advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, algorithms, and formal criteria for parsing terms and formulas, for defining substitution safety, for the structure of formal deductions, and for identification of definability via automorphisms in first-order logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphism preserves definable relations (Corollary 22E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let h be an automorphism of the structure A, and let R be an n-ary relation on |A| definable in A. Then for any a1, . . . , an in |A|, (a1, . . . , an) ∈ R ⇔ (h(a1), . . . , h(an)) ∈ R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an immediate consequence of the homomorphism theorem. Use it to show that any automorphism of A must preserve relations that are definable in A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for showing non-definability via automorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If there exists an automorphism of a structure that does not preserve a given subset or relation, then that subset/relation cannot be definable in the structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: in (R;<) the strictly increasing map h(a)=a^3 maps points outside N into N, so N is not definable; in a vector space (E; +, f_r) the doubling map x↦2x is an automorphism that does not preserve unit vectors, so 'unit vectors' is not definable. Strategy: produce an automorphism moving a witness of the property to a non-witness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and assignment of K for parsing
rubrics_metrics.description: Define K(s)=1−n where n is the number of terms (for term symbols) or required following objects (for formula symbols); specific assignments include K(x)=1, K(c)=1, K(f)=1−n for n-place function symbol f; for formula-symbols K(() = −1, K()) = 1, K(∀) = −1, K(¬) = 0, K(→) = −1, K(P) = 1−n for n-place predicate symbol P, K(=) = −1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend K additively over concatenations: K(s1...sn)=ΣK(si). K is chosen so that K(term)=1 and K(wff)=1, making the K-function the central tool for parsing and unique readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term legality criterion via K
rubrics_metrics.description: An expression ε (built from variables, constants, and function symbols) is a term iff K(ε)=1 and for every terminal segment ε' of ε we have K(ε')>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stronger statement (J´askowski): if K(ε')>0 for every terminal segment then ε is a concatenation of K(ε) terms. Corollary: no proper initial segment of a term is itself a term (since K of any proper initial segment is <1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parsing algorithm for terms (constructive criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: To decide whether an expression is a term and construct its parse tree: iteratively expand minimal vertices; if a minimal vertex has a single symbol (variable or constant) accept; otherwise the first symbol must be an n-place function symbol f (n>0), create n children and scan after f to find the first string t with K(t)=1 to place at the leftmost child; repeat until done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection conditions: if the first symbol encountered is not a variable/constant at a minimal vertex, reject; if scanning after f reaches the end before finding a t with K(t)=1, reject. The algorithm ensures uniqueness by selecting the earliest t with K(t)=1 (Corollary 23C prevents alternate decompositions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Readability Theorem for terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of terms is freely generated from the set of variables and constant symbols by the operations F_f (for function symbols f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: there is a unique tree demonstrating how a term is built from its symbols; the K-function machinery underlies uniqueness. Proof uses that ranges of F_f are pairwise disjoint and Corollary 23C to prevent ambiguous initial segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wff legality criterion via K (formulas)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any well-formed formula (wff) α, K(α)=1, and no proper initial segment of a wff is itself a wff (i.e., for any proper initial segment α' of α, K(α')<1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemmas 23D and 23E establish K(α)=1 and K(α')<1 for proper initial segments; Corollary 23F: no proper initial segment of a formula is itself a formula. These facts parallel the term-case and support unique parsing of formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parsing algorithm / Unique Readability Theorem for formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Wffs are freely generated from atomic formulas by the operations E¬, E→, and Qi (quantifier-operations). A formula parse is obtained by treating atomic formulas as minimal vertices and applying the analogous tree-construction procedure (handling leading ∀ vi and parentheses/¬ appropriately).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-atomic wffs that begin with ∀ vi there is one child; if begin with ( then inspect next symbol to decide if it's ¬ or a binary → form; K-function or parenthesis counting locates the correct split. This guarantees unique decomposition into construction operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for formal proofs/deductions
rubrics_metrics.description: A satisfactory proof (deduction) must be finitely long and effectively checkable; the set of formulas provable without hypotheses should be effectively enumerable (decidable-checkability of proofs and enumerability of validities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements motivate the deductive calculus presented and imply that compactness and enumerability are necessary (and with the presented calculus, sufficient) for existence of proofs/deductions establishing logical implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a deduction (formal)
rubrics_metrics.description: A deduction of ϕ from Γ is a finite sequence α0,...,αn of formulas with αn = ϕ such that for each k≤n either (a) αk ∈ Γ ∪ Λ (where Λ is the set of logical axioms), or (b) αk is obtained by modus ponens from two earlier formulas in the sequence (i.e., for some i,j<k, αj is αi → αk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation: Γ ⊢ ϕ means ϕ is deducible from Γ. Equivalently, theorems of Γ are formulas obtainable from Γ ∪ Λ by repeated application of modus ponens. Deductions can be viewed as linearized derivation trees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of inference: modus ponens (single rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The calculus uses one rule of inference: from α and α → β infer β (modus ponens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The set of theorems is obtained by closing Γ ∪ Λ under repeated application of modus ponens. The system intentionally uses an infinite axiom set with only this single rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical axioms organized in six groups (what qualifies as an axiom)
rubrics_metrics.description: Logical axioms are all generalizations (universal closures) of wffs of the following forms (where x,y are variables and α,β wffs): (1) tautologies (from sentential logic using prime formulas), (2) ∀x α → α[x:=t] (with substitutability condition), (3) ∀x(α → β) → (∀x α → ∀x β), (4) α → ∀x α when x not free in α, and if equality in language then (5) x = x, (6) x = y → (α → α[x↦y]) where α is atomic and α[x↦y] replaces zero or more occurrences of x by y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups 3–6 are standard and largely self-explanatory; groups 1 and 2 require special attention (tautologies are formed by treating prime formulas as sentential atoms; group 2 requires the substitutability restriction to avoid variable capture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitutability criterion for ∀x α → α[x:=t] (axiom group 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A term t is substitutable for x in α (so that ∀x α → α[x:=t] is an axiom-generalization) iff: (1) for atomic α, any t is substitutable; (2) t is substitutable for x in ¬α iff it is substitutable in α, and in (α→β) iff it is substitutable in both α and β; (3) t is substitutable for x in ∀y α iff either x does not occur free in ∀y α, or y does not occur in t and t is substitutable for x in α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recursive definition prevents quantifier capture (illustrated by the hazardous example where naive substitution yields an almost-always false sentence). Even if t is not substitutable, α[x:=t] can still be formed syntactically, but it is not an instance admissible as an axiom without the substitutability condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of tautologies as axiom group 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Axiom group 1 consists of generalizations of tautologies of sentential logic obtained by taking prime formulas (atomic formulas and formulas of the form ∀x α) as sentential atoms; any sentential tautology (with only ¬ and →) built from these prime formulas belongs to group 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, tautologies of sentential logic become first-order logical axioms by treating prime formulas as sentence symbols; example provided: ∀x[(∀y ¬Py → ¬Px) → (Px → ¬∀y ¬Py)].

rubrics_metrics.name: Induction principle for deductions (closure criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If S is a set of wffs that includes Γ ∪ Λ and is closed under modus ponens, then S contains every theorem of Γ (i.e., every formula deducible from Γ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a method to argue that a candidate set S correctly contains all deducible formulas: verify it contains axioms and hypotheses and is closed under the single inference rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic rejection criteria for parsing
rubrics_metrics.description: During parsing, reject an expression as a non-term if at a minimal vertex the symbol is not a variable/constant or if after selecting an n-place function symbol f you fail to find a terminal string t with K(t)=1 before the end of the expression; similarly for formulas, fail when the expected K=1 segment cannot be located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operational rejection conditions ensure the parsing algorithm halts with either a valid parse tree or a certificate of non-term/non-formula.
